title: Julia de Burgos's birth chart
metaDescription: Julia de Burgos's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 28.2° Aquarius. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: 0.4° separates Venus and Pluto from an exact trine; at that range taste and depth read as one mechanism. A trine runs downhill — the talent that never announces itself because it never had to.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: At noon on that date the Sun stood at 28.2° Aquarius, inside the third decan (20°–30°), whose traditional sub-ruler is Venus. The decan is the older, finer division — it is what the sign looks like once you stop rounding it to thirty degrees.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: Mercury holds 14.9° Pisces, Mars holds 5.8° Cancer — in the old shorthand, thought steeped in tone and memory; effort that surges when it matters.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Venus and Pluto hold the closest angle here — a trine, 0.4° wide. A trine runs downhill — the talent that never announces itself because it never had to. Behind it, the Sun trine Pluto at 1.0°, and the Sun conjunction Venus at 1.4° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. The unknown hour cannot unmake any of this: every aspect named survived all twenty-five samples of the day.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: The Moon makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The oldest layer of the scheme — seven planets, four conditions — flags three placements in this chart. The Sun in Aquarius at 28.2° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Mercury in Pisces at 14.9° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Mars in Cancer at 5.8° is in fall. Dignity is a statement about conditions, not about worth.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Counting only the 8 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the chart runs 5 air, 3 water by element and 3 fixed, 3 mutable, 2 cardinal by modality. Venus crossed from Aquarius into Pisces during that day, so its sign is left open. No settled placement falls in fire or earth — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — the optical reversal the tradition reads as review — energy turned over before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Scorpio into Sagittarius during that day at the birthplace, travelling 13.7° between one midnight and the next. Half the day belongs to each sign, and the split falls at an unrecorded hour — so this page holds the Moon as a genuine unknown.
